usageNotes: Use this to gracefully (or forcefully) shut down all VMs and containers on a specific node — typically before a planned node maintenance window, hardware reboot, or controlled power-off. The `vms` parameter lets you limit the scope to specific VMIDs instead of everything on the node. By default, each guest gets 180 seconds to shut down cleanly before a hard-stop is forced; lower `timeout` or set `force-stop` to false if you want a pure graceful-only approach. Returns a task UPID you can poll to track overall completion.

examples.summary: Stop all guests on node pve1 with a 5-minute timeout and hard-stop fallback

destructiveReason: Sends a shutdown (or hard-stop) signal to every running VM and container on the target node, causing immediate service disruption and potential data loss for guests that do not gracefully handle ACPI shutdown.
tips: Use the `vms` parameter (comma-separated VMIDs) to stop a subset of guests without touching the rest of the node.
The returned string is a UPID — poll it via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to know when all stop tasks have completed.
max-workers caps parallel stop tasks; keeping it low (2–4) reduces I/O contention during flushing and is safer for storage-heavy guests.
force-stop defaults to true (1); explicitly set it to false if you need a strictly graceful shutdown with no hard-kill fallback.
